Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Football | National Asante Kotoko suffer defeat against Bechem United on Stanley Menzo’s debut Source : JoySports 22 November 2026 5:06pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Bechem United claimed a hard-fought 1-0 victory over Asante Kotoko in Ghana Premier League Matchday 12, with Isaac Korankye scoring the decisive goal at the Nana Fosu Gyeabour Park.
Korankye, making his first start of the season, headed home in the 63rd minute to hand the Hunters all three points and spoil Stanley Menzo's first match in charge of the Porcupine Warriors.
Menzo, who was appointed head coach for the remainder of the 2026/27 campaign just three days before the encounter, was tasked with reviving Kotoko's struggling league campaign following a disappointing run of results under interim coach Hamza Obeng.
The visitors started brightly, with Hubert Gyau winning a free-kick in the Bechem half in the fifth minute. Emmanuel Sanja delivered the set-piece and found Richard Boadu, but the midfielder failed to make proper contact with the ball.
Kotoko continued to search for an opening, with Lawson Kyei Manu setting up Eric Gbetta in the penalty area in the 23rd minute, only for his effort to be blocked.
Bechem also threatened, and Samuel Okai came close to breaking the deadlock in the 30th minute when his effort flashed narrowly wide of the post.
The first half, which also saw Bechem's Baba Moro Abdulai and Kotoko's Umar Ali receive yellow cards, ended goalless despite promising moments from both sides.
Menzo introduced Opoku Agyemang at the break in place of Emmanuel Mamah as Kotoko looked to add more attacking threat.
However, the visitors struggled to turn their possession into clear-cut opportunities. A promising opening came in the 52nd minute when Umar Ali released Opoku inside the box, but the substitute's left-footed effort lacked the power to trouble Bechem goalkeeper Benjamin Asiedu.
The breakthrough arrived in the 63rd minute when Korankye rose highest to power a header into the net and give the hosts the lead.
Bechem nearly doubled their advantage four minutes later, but Kotoko goalkeeper Aziz Dari Haruna produced an excellent save to prevent the Hunters from extending their lead.
Kotoko made further changes in an attempt to rescue the game, introducing Derrick Anthony Duah, Seth Kwadwo and Solomon Asaah, while Bechem also made substitutions to protect their advantage.
Asante Kotoko pushed for an equaliser in the closing stages, with Asaah directing a header towards goal in the 86th minute, but the Bechem goalkeeper was equal to the task.
The hosts' resolve was tested further in stoppage time when Afranie Mensah was sent off for a foul on Asaah, leaving Bechem with 10 men for the closing moments.
Despite the numerical disadvantage, the Hunters defended resolutely to preserve their slender lead and secure a memorable victory.
The result represents a disappointing start to Menzo's tenure as head coach, with Kotoko missing the opportunity to improve their position in the league standings as they continue their pursuit of the leading sides.
